concepts.term: Practical application of an electromagnetic wave
concepts.def: A use made of one group of the electromagnetic spectrum. The specification lists radio waves with television and radio; microwaves with satellite communications and cooking food; infrared with electrical heaters, cooking food and infrared cameras; visible light with fibre optic communications; ultraviolet with energy efficient lamps and sun tanning; and X-rays and gamma rays with medical imaging and treatments.

Radio waves are the longest-wavelength group of the spectrum and are used to broadcast television and radio programmes. A transmitter converts the signal into radio waves, and an aerial on a house or a receiver picks them up and converts them back.

concepts.term: Microwaves – satellite communications and cooking food
concepts.def: Microwaves have shorter wavelengths than radio waves. They are used to carry signals up to satellites and back down to earth, and in a microwave oven, where they are absorbed by the food and increase its energy store.

Infrared is emitted by all objects, and by more the hotter they are. It is used in electrical heaters and grills, where it is absorbed by the surface it falls on, and in infrared cameras, which form an image from the infrared an object emits.
Visible light is the narrow band of the spectrum the eye detects. In fibre optic communications, information is sent as very rapid pulses of light that travel along a thin glass fibre.

concepts.term: Ultraviolet – energy efficient lamps and sun tanning
concepts.def: Ultraviolet has shorter wavelengths than visible light. It is produced inside an energy efficient (fluorescent) lamp and converted to visible light by the coating on the tube, and it is used in sunbeds and sunlight to tan skin, though it can damage skin cells.

concepts.term: X-rays and gamma rays – medical imaging and treatments
concepts.def: X-rays and gamma rays are the shortest-wavelength groups. They are used to make images of the inside of the body, because bone absorbs them far more than soft tissue does, and in treatment, where a beam is directed at a tumour to destroy its cells.

concepts.term: Absorption and transmission decide the use (HT)
concepts.def: Whether a wave is suitable for an application depends on what absorbs it and what lets it through. Microwaves suit satellite links because the atmosphere transmits them; infrared suits a grill because food absorbs it; X-rays suit imaging because bone absorbs them and flesh does not.

The layer on the inside of an energy efficient lamp that absorbs the ultraviolet produced in the tube and re-emits the energy as visible light, so the lamp lights the room without releasing ultraviolet into it.

mcqs.q: The specification lists a practical application for each group of electromagnetic waves. Which pairing is correct?
options: Satellite communication uses radio waves
Sun tanning lamps mainly give out infrared
Fibre optic communications use visible light
A toaster cooks bread using microwaves
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs visible light with fibre optic communications: the signal travels along the glass fibre as rapid pulses of light.

mcqs.q: Which use does the specification give for radio waves?
options: Broadcasting television and radio programmes
Sending signals to and from satellites in orbit
Carrying signals along fibre optic cables
Taking images of bones inside the body
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs radio waves with television and radio.

mcqs.q: A signal is sent from a ground station up to a satellite in orbit and then back down to a second ground station. Which waves carry the signal?
options: Radio waves, which are used for broadcasting today
Microwaves, which pass through the atmosphere
Infrared, which is given out by all hot objects
Visible light, which goes in straight lines
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs microwaves with satellite communications; the atmosphere transmits them, so they reach the satellite and return.

mcqs.q: How does a microwave oven cook food?
options: Microwaves heat the middle of the food first
Microwaves make the food slightly radioactive
An element's red glow is the infrared that cooks it
The food absorbs microwaves and heats up
mcqs.explain: Microwaves are absorbed by the food, and the energy transferred raises its temperature.

mcqs.q: An electric grill glows red and cooks the food placed underneath it. Which radiation transfers energy to the food?
options: Microwaves, because all cookers use microwaves
Infrared, which is absorbed by the food surface
Ultraviolet, because the element glows white
Radio waves, because they carry heat energy
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs infrared with electrical heaters and cooking food; the hot element emits infrared, which the surface of the food absorbs.

mcqs.q: An infrared camera is used to find a person standing in a dark field at night. Why does the person show up on the image?
options: The camera shines visible light on the person
Infrared from the body can be seen by the eye too
The person reflects ultraviolet from the night sky above
Their body gives out infrared that the camera detects
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs infrared with infrared cameras; a warm body emits infrared, which the camera detects even in total darkness.

mcqs.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave carries the signals in a fibre optic cable?
options: Visible light, sent as very rapid pulses
Microwaves, as used for satellite phone links
Radio waves, as used for television aerials
Infrared, which warms the glass fibre
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs visible light with fibre optic communications; information travels as pulses of light along the glass fibre.

mcqs.q: A sunbed is used to give a tan. Which statement about the radiation it uses is correct?
options: It gives out infrared, and the heat browns skin
It gives out visible light, which the skin absorbs
It gives out ultraviolet, which can harm skin
Its ultraviolet is safe because the dose is small
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs ultraviolet with sun tanning; ultraviolet darkens the skin but is absorbed by skin cells and can damage them.

mcqs.q: Why does a broken bone show up clearly on an X-ray photograph?
options: X-rays pass through bone but are absorbed by flesh
X-rays are reflected from the surface of the bone
X-rays make the bone give out light of its own
X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone
mcqs.explain: Bone absorbs X-rays far more strongly than flesh does, so a shadow of the bone, and of the break in it, falls on the detector.

mcqs.q: Gamma rays are used in hospitals to treat cancer. Which statement is correct?
options: Gamma rays leave the treated tissue permanently radioactive
Gamma rays are far too dangerous ever to be used here
A beam of gamma rays is aimed at the tumour to kill cells
Gamma rays are used only to photograph broken bones
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs X-rays and gamma rays with medical treatments; a directed beam destroys the cells of the tumour.

mcqs.q: (HT only) Explain why microwaves rather than infrared are used to send signals to a communications satellite.
options: Microwaves travel much faster through space than infrared can
Microwaves pass through the atmosphere, infrared does not
Infrared cannot cross the vacuum of space, but microwaves do
Microwaves are the only waves a dish aerial can send
mcqs.explain: The atmosphere transmits microwaves, so the signal reaches the satellite and returns; infrared is strongly absorbed by gases and water vapour in the air.

mcqs.q: (HT only) An energy efficient lamp produces ultraviolet inside its tube, yet the room is lit by visible light. Which explanation is correct?
options: A coating absorbs ultraviolet and emits visible light
The lamp is designed to send ultraviolet into the room
The ultraviolet itself is the light you see the room by
Ultraviolet slows down in the tube, becoming visible light
mcqs.explain: The fluorescent coating on the inside of the tube absorbs the ultraviolet and re-emits the energy as visible light, so the room is lit without ultraviolet leaving the lamp.
